# Draft:International American School of Warsaw

}}
The International American School of Warsaw (IAS) is a private international school in the Ursynów district of Warsaw, Poland, founded in 1989. It serves students from kindergarten through grade 12.
The school is accredited by the International Baccalaureate Organization, Cognia, and the Polish Ministry of National Education. Upper school students may pursue the IB Diploma Programme, an American high school diploma, or the Polish Matura.
Campus
The school occupies two buildings on ulica Dembego, near the Kabaty metro station and the Kabaty Woods. The lower school operates from Dembego 12 and the upper school from Dembego 18.
Academics
The language of instruction is English. Students may also study Polish, German, or French. A Polish as a Second Language programme is available for non-Polish-speaking students, and an English as an Additional Language programme supports non-native English speakers.
In a 2023 interview, then-principal Matthew Krasner stated that roughly half of graduates attend universities outside Poland, with the remainder enrolling in Polish institutions.
Student life
The school publishes a student newspaper, The IAS Times. In November 2025, IAS hosted its first Model United Nations conference.
